summary: Add an owner-only worker operation and CLI for sanitized Naver top-bar structure capture, recover dead auth-store locks, and close MCP client keys on every exit path.
verification: npx vitest run test/unit/agent-auth-store.test.mjs test/unit/agent-mcp-client.test.mjs test/unit/agent-ipc.test.mjs test/unit/agent-worker.test.mjs test/unit/agent-runtime.test.mjs test/unit/agent-mcp.test.mjs test/unit/agent-naver-login-status.test.mjs test/unit/agent-naver-topbar.test.mjs
risks: The operator-only capture must remain unavailable through MCP and must return no page text or unsanitized iframe URL data.
Stale-lock recovery must remove only an owned regular 0600 lock whose recorded PID is confirmed gone.

tasks.title: Add operator-only Naver top-bar capture
tasks.change: Allow operator.naver.topbar_structure only on the owner-only worker socket; navigate a worker-owned page under loginStatusPolicy(), serialize selected top-bar DOM with text and aria-label redaction and an element cap, expose a private CLI that writes mode 0600 output, and prove MCP/gateway cannot call it.
tasks.effect: The operator CLI writes sanitized structure while the MCP tool catalog and dispatcher cannot reach the operation.

verification.risk_reason: A DOM leak or accidental gateway exposure could reveal profile data or widen the authenticated API.
verification.test_reason: The existing suite does not cover this operation or sanitizer; fixture-based canaries and gateway denial need repeatable regression checks.
verification.subject: sanitized operator capture and MCP boundary
verification.procedure: Unit-test a DOM fixture with fake identity and cookie-like text, exercise worker IPC dispatch, and call the MCP/gateway with the operator operation name.
verification.pass_criterion: Only permitted sanitized markup returns, output is capped, and MCP/gateway never dispatch the operator operation.

tasks.title: Recover only dead owned auth-store locks
tasks.change: Write the owner PID into each writer lock and retry acquisition once only after confirming that an owned regular 0600 lock names a dead PID.
tasks.effect: A dead-owner lock can be recovered, while a live-owner lock remains exclusive.

verification.risk_reason: Incorrect recovery could let concurrent writers replace authentication state or keys.
verification.test_reason: Existing storage tests cover lock exclusion but not stale owner recovery or PID metadata.
verification.subject: dead and live writer lock behavior
verification.procedure: Create a mode 0600 lock with an impossible PID, then one with the current live PID; open the key store in each case.
verification.pass_criterion: The dead lock is replaced by a lock containing the current PID, and the live lock still fails with STATE_UNSAFE.

tasks.title: Close MCP key stores and preserve known gateway errors
tasks.change: Close client key stores from client close and stdio-client finally/signal paths, and preserve known gateway auth/read error codes from either parsed error data.code or error.code.
tasks.effect: Client shutdown always releases key-store locks and known gateway failures retain their public code.

verification.risk_reason: An unclosed key-store lock blocks future clients, and error-code loss hides version and authorization failures.
verification.test_reason: The current tests do not assert signal cleanup or VERSION_UNSUPPORTED passthrough from an HTTP error response.
verification.subject: MCP key-store cleanup and gateway error passthrough
verification.procedure: Exercise normal, error, and signal stdio exits plus a gateway response carrying VERSION_UNSUPPORTED in error.data.code.
verification.pass_criterion: The key-store lock is released on every exit and known error codes survive; unknown codes become AUTH_INVALID.
